primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12926324/ (Vitamin D section, table entry for hospitalized COVID-19 patients)
assessment: Peanut oil was the vehicle in both the high-dose vitamin D3 and placebo arms of a COVID-19 study summarized in the review. That contrast cannot distinguish peanut oil and does not report a refined-peanut-oil effect on smell.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5107643/ (MEG preprocessing and visuomotor task methods)
assessment: NUTMEG is the software used to filter magnetoencephalographic data. The case-control study evaluates visually guided movement in schizophrenia without any ground nutmeg or apathy intervention.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6796240/ (Schwabl human stool microplastics pilot, Introduction and Methods)
assessment: The presenter cites shrimp among marine foods previously found to contain microplastics. The eight-person study enumerates microplastics in stool and documents exposure practices, without testing boiled shrimp or measuring falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7545776/ (Cuttlefish prey-catching presentation, shrimp skewer recording)
assessment: Shrimp appears as prey offered on a motor-controlled skewer while cuttlefish body patterns are recorded. The investigators assess predatory behavior and not fall frequency in patients.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8551951/ (Freshwater shrimp antimicrobial-peptide, hemocyanin and osmoregulation presentations)
assessment: Shrimp are study organisms in the presentations on immune responses, hemocyanin or gill physiology. The measured outcomes belong to laboratory shrimp models and have no human falls comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5253238/ (MAOA sequencing methods, PCR product cleanup)
assessment: Shrimp alkaline phosphatase is a sequencing reagent in a study of human MAOA variants. The design is a mutation screen and supplies no boiled-shrimp or falls measurement.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1490295/ (SGIM tracking ID 134821, steamed shrimp case; separate ambulatory older-adult falls presentations)
assessment: A single autoimmune hepatitis case reported prior steamed-shrimp intake. The older-adult falls presentations separately evaluate such exposures as medication use and functional status, without a dietary shrimp comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3063356/ (Discussion of desiccation-tolerant organisms)
assessment: Brine shrimp are cited as a comparative group of organisms that can tolerate desiccation. The article evaluates bacterial oxidative-stress resistance rather than human shrimp intake and fall frequency.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3309362/ (Introduction, aquatic hosts; Results on temperature-dependent bacterial phenotypes)
assessment: Shrimp appear among aquatic hosts in the introductory ecology of Vibrio coralliilyticus. The original experiments examine temperature-dependent bacterial phenotypes, with no clinical exposure or falls measure.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4107077/ (Genotyping procedures and PET placebo-analgesia methods)
assessment: Shrimp alkaline phosphatase is used in genotype processing. Participant outcomes concern placebo analgesia and brain activity and are not related to shrimp consumption.

primary_locator: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25238997/ (PubMed author abstract; DOI 10.1007/s11307-014-0791-7)
assessment: The commentary describes consistency of quantitative human PET measurements for three different tracers and contrasts the approach with phantom tests. The indexed PMC accession is a different conference DOI, and the true abstract gives no dietary exposure or falls study.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4408443/ (Bone marrow mesenchymal cells, extracellular vesicles and progeroid model presentation)
assessment: Shrimp luciferase is an imaging reporter used to follow transplanted mouse cells in a conference study of cell survival and aging. The shrimp reference is a reporter source without a cooked-food or falls comparison.

primary_locator: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26387020/ (PubMed author abstract; DOI 10.3168/jds.2015-9445)
assessment: The author abstract sets out reporting guidelines and a checklist for dairy cattle reproductive intervention studies. The linked PMC resolves to a separate conference collection, and the original abstract does not concern shrimp or human falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6247239/ (Pentraxin 3 in shrimp allergy, white shrimp enzyme and shrimp disease presentations)
assessment: The identified shrimp presentations concern mast-cell and mouse allergy responses or shrimp enzymes and disease. None of those study designs tests boiled shrimp as an intervention for patient fall frequency.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8061271/ (Reference period definitions and lake charr feeding ecology discussion)
assessment: Fall denotes the September to November season when analyzing fish growth. Mysis is an invertebrate prey of one lake charr ecotype, and the article does not concern clinical falls.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13441361/ (Ambient ionization in food analysis and minced-shrimp authentication reference)
assessment: Minced shrimp is a food sample authenticated with mass spectrometry. The reviewed outcomes concern sample identity and chemical characterization, without human dietary fall outcomes.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13436250/ (Marine-derived compound tables, shrimp source entries)
assessment: The review lists shrimp as a source of extracted candidate compounds in marine neuroprotection research. It does not compare boiled-shrimp consumption with a patient fall outcome.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4070603/ (UEG P1106, P1678 and P1005)
assessment: P1106 studies EVOO phenols and inflammatory responses in cultured macrophages. P1678 examines oil-based lipids and leukocytes. P1005 studies swallowing-related feedback in severe dysphagia as a separate protocol without an EVOO intervention.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4669991/ (UEG P0633 hepatic lipid peroxidation table and liver fibrosis studies)
assessment: Olive oil is administered as a vehicle or experimental control in the collection’s liver toxicity and fibrosis presentations. P0633 reports hepatic outcomes after carbon tetrachloride, without a dietary oil swallowing measure.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5613494/ (Historical index entries, dysphagia and olive oil)
assessment: The collection index records cases of dysphagia in one entry and a report on the purgative use of olive oil in another. The separate entries do not document a dietary extra-virgin olive oil swallowing comparison.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6153547/ (Presentations 1 and 3930, and the rosemary hand-temperature comparison)
assessment: The dysphagia case describes hypnosis with graded exposure to feared foods after cervical surgery. A separate qualitative report characterizes black olive oil consumption in breast cancer survivors, and oil is a comparator in a hand-temperature demonstration.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6157254/ (Presentation P21 and separate PSAND translation or validation presentation)
assessment: Ozonized EVOO is a topical comparator for pressure ulcers in P21. A different study assesses a swallowing evaluation protocol in acute stroke, with no edible-oil contrast.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6796246/ (Cirrhosis model, aortic 5-HT2A vascular reactivity presentation)
assessment: Olive oil was given to control rats in a carbon tetrachloride cirrhosis model. The reported contrast is on isolated aortic responses and is unrelated to dietary EVOO and swallowing severity.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7672678/ (UEG P0635 alternative intravenous lipid emulsions and P0527 poststroke dysphagia)
assessment: The olive-oil emulsion in P0635 is administered intravenously to patients receiving parenteral nutrition, with hospital outcomes. P0527 separately tests pharyngeal cortical activation after stroke.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2936955/ (Mitochondrial pathways, Mohr–Tranebjaerg and antioxidant lipid sections)
assessment: The review discusses dysphagia as part of Mohr–Tranebjaerg syndrome. The olive or sunflower oil studies concern vitamin E plus dietary fats and mitochondrial oxidative markers in animals, without a swallowing endpoint.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7117565/ (Adverse events and database search strategy)
assessment: The omega-3 review notes some participants withdrawing because capsule size made swallowing difficult. Olive oil is listed as a search term and the cited dysphagia events do not compare extra-virgin olive oil diets.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6390820/ (Participants and eligibility; Discussion on dietary fats)
assessment: Dysphagia is an exclusion criterion in the multiple sclerosis nutrition study. Olive oil is mentioned among sources of dietary fat in other dietary patterns and the study does not measure its effect on swallowing.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7972945/ (ISGCON poster P. pentosaceus I44 and separate esophageal dysphagia reports)
assessment: Olive and sesame oils were tested on bacterial culture properties including acid tolerance. Separate congress cases and procedures describe esophageal dysphagia, without the bacterial study's olive-oil exposure.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12327234/ (SEMO oral communication 20 and separate oral mucositis study)
assessment: The ozonated-olive-oil case series uses topical products on oral lichen planus and describes lesion or general symptom changes. Separate mucositis and medication studies refer to dysphagia without an EVOO contrast.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12457634/ (Chrono Med-Diet Score bone-density presentation and axial spondyloarthritis diet presentation)
assessment: Olive-oil use is an item in conference reports on bone mineral density and dietary practices in rheumatology. These outcomes do not measure swallowing difficulty during an isolated oil intervention.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13042604/ (Table on wellness components and acupuncture section)
assessment: Olive oil is listed within overall Mediterranean or MIND nutrition. Dysphagia appears as a nutrition barrier and a possible response in acupuncture research, with no separate dietary EVOO swallowing result.

primary_locator: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3534347/ (ECR presentation B606 and separate group reporting pelvic symptoms)
assessment: Sunflower oil was heated as a test fluid in a CT phantom. Urinary urgency is reported in a separate pelvic clinical presentation and was not measured in relation to dietary refined sunflower oil.
